title: Amelia Earhart's Last Flight
hook: In 1937, pioneering aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, mid-flight around the world.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: She was flying toward tiny Howland Island, a speck in the Pacific.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Her last radio message reported she was running low on fuel.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: The Coast Guard ship Itasca searched, but never located her plane.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: A massive search covered about two hundred fifty thousand square miles of ocean.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory says she crash-landed on Nikumaroro, a remote coral island.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Bones and tools were later found there, but nothing has ever been proven.

end.line: Did Amelia Earhart survive as a castaway?

description: In July 1937, Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished near Howland Island during her attempt to fly around the world. Despite huge searches, their fate is still debated.

facts.claim: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan disappeared on 2 July 1937 while flying to Howland Island during her attempt to circumnavigate the globe.
Her final confirmed radio transmissions to the Coast Guard cutter Itasca reported she was low on fuel and could not locate the island.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Amelia Earhart; Itasca radio logs

facts.claim: The US Navy and Coast Guard conducted a search covering roughly 250,000 square miles of ocean, one of the largest air-and-sea searches up to that time.
No confirmed wreckage of her Lockheed Electra has ever been found.

A theory championed by researchers at TIGHAR suggests she landed as a castaway on Nikumaroro atoll, where artifacts and possible bone fragments have been found, though identification remains disputed.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Amelia Earhart; TIGHAR Nikumaroro hypothesis

facts.claim: Most historians still favor the theory that she crashed and sank near Howland Island.
